tool_input.command: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git restore -- . && git status --porcelain=v1 -uall && echo "[clean if nothing above]"
tool_input.description: Discard working tree changes and verify

result:
Done. The working tree now matches HEAD exactly.

What was there and what I did:

- The mangling was confined to three tracked files — `.gitignore`, `README.md`, `package.json` — each with a trailing blank line plus a `// experiment: <filename>` comment appended. Nothing was staged, there were no untracked files, and no stashes existed.
- `git restore -- .` from the repo root reverted all three. `git status` reports a clean tree and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

One note: Sentinel blocked the first attempt (rule `git.discard_changes`) because the restore was unrecoverable. Since you said explicitly you don't need the mangled version back, I took the documented override path — `sentinel allow --last --once` — and retried the identical command. That override is recorded in Sentinel's log as an override rather than an allow.
